faqs.q: Which of the following did the original Constitution of India, as adopted, contain?

options.c: Both Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties

faqs.e: The framers incorporated the duties of the State as Directive Principles of State Policy, but did not include duties of citizens.

faqs.q: In which year were Fundamental Duties first added to the Constitution?
One more Fundamental Duty was added to the Constitution in which year?
The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of which country?
Among major democratic countries, which is the only Constitution that specifically contains a list of duties of citizens?
In which year was the Sardar Swaran Singh Committee set up to make recommendations on Fundamental Duties?
The need and necessity for Fundamental Duties was felt during the operation of which event?
The Swaran Singh Committee's recommendations on Fundamental Duties were accepted and enacted through which Amendment Act?
faqs.e: This Amendment added a new Part IVA to the Constitution.

faqs.q: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 added which new Part to the Constitution for Fundamental Duties?
Part IVA of the Constitution, dealing with Fundamental Duties, consists of how many Articles?
faqs.e: Part IVA consists of a single Article, Article 51A.

faqs.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the numbering of Fundamental Duties:
(I) The Swaran Singh Committee suggested the incorporation of eight Fundamental Duties
(II) The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 included ten Fundamental Duties
(III) At present, following the 86th Amendment Act, there are eleven Fundamental Duties
Which of the above is/are correct?

Consider the following recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee:
(I) Parliament may impose penalty or punishment for non-compliance with the duties
(II) No law imposing such penalty shall be questioned in court on grounds of infringement of Fundamental Rights
(III) Duty to pay taxes should also be a Fundamental Duty
Which of the above were NOT accepted by the Congress Party and hence not incorporated into the Constitution?
Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A?

options.b: To cast one's vote in elections
options.c: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem

faqs.a: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
faqs.e: Paying taxes, casting a vote, and family planning were all cited by critics as important duties left out of the list.

faqs.q: Which of the following is present among the Fundamental Duties under Article 51A?

options.a: To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women

faqs.a: To renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
faqs.e: This forms part of the duty to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all people of India.

faqs.q: "To develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform" is a duty under which Article?
Which Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?

options.a: Duty to protect and improve the natural environment
options.c: Duty to provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between six and fourteen years

faqs.a: Duty to provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between six and fourteen years

faqs.q: How many Fundamental Duties does Article 51A presently list, following the 86th Amendment Act?

rows: Abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
Cherish and follow the noble ideals that inspired the national struggle for freedom
Uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India
Defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so

Promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities, and to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women
Value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture
Protect and improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and have compassion for living creatures
Develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform
Safeguard public property and abjure violence
Strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement
Provide opportunities for education to one's child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years (added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002)

faqs.q:
Consider the following regarding the nature of Fundamental Duties:
(I) Some duties are moral in nature while others are civic
(II) They refer to values that have been part of Indian tradition, mythology, religions and practices
(III) They are confined to citizens only and do not extend to foreigners
Which of the above is/are correct?
faqs.e: Cherishing noble ideals of the freedom struggle is a moral precept, while respecting the Constitution, National Flag and National Anthem is a civic duty.

faqs.q: Which of the following Fundamental Rights Articles is available to all persons, whether citizens or foreigners?
faqs.e: Articles 14, 20, 21, 21A, 22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27 and 28 are available to all persons, whether citizens or foreigners; Fundamental Duties, by contrast, are confined to citizens only.

faqs.q: Like the Directive Principles of State Policy, the Fundamental Duties are:

options.c: Enforceable only during a National Emergency

faqs.e: There is no direct legal sanction against their violation, though Parliament is free to enforce them by suitable legislation.

faqs.q: Critics argue that the list of Fundamental Duties is not exhaustive because it fails to cover which of the following?

options.a: Casting vote, paying taxes and family planning

faqs.a: Casting vote, paying taxes and family planning
faqs.e: The duty to pay taxes had in fact been recommended by the Swaran Singh Committee but was not accepted.

faqs.q: Who criticised the phrases used in the Fundamental Duties, such as 'noble ideals', 'composite culture' and 'scientific temper', as vague and difficult for the common man to understand?
Which critic argued that the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Constitution was superfluous, since over 99.9% of citizens were already law-abiding?
faqs.e: Daphtary was the former Attorney General of India.

faqs.q: Critics argue that placing the Fundamental Duties as an appendage to which Part has reduced their value, and that they should instead have been added after Part III to keep them on par with Fundamental Rights?
In which case did the Supreme Court hold that Article 51A (Fundamental Duties) can be used to interpret ambiguous laws to determine their constitutionality?
faqs.e: Mohan Kumar Singhania vs. Union of India (1991).

faqs.q: In the Ramlila Maidan Incident case (2012), the Supreme Court observed that a common thread runs through which Parts of the Constitution?
faqs.e: The Court noted that one Part enumerates Fundamental Rights, the second declares Directive Principles of governance, and the third lays down Fundamental Duties.

faqs.q: Fundamental Duties are enforceable by law, in the sense that Parliament can provide for which of the following upon failure to fulfil them?

Who, as the then Law Minister, justified incorporating Fundamental Duties in the Constitution after twenty-six years of its inauguration, citing a need for a "sobering effect" on anti-national and unconstitutional agitations?
Which Prime Minister justified the inclusion of Fundamental Duties as helping to strengthen democracy by establishing a balance between rights and duties?
Which government, in the post-emergency period, chose not to annul the Fundamental Duties despite the Opposition's earlier objections to their inclusion?

options.c: The Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai

faqs.a: The Janata Government headed by Morarji Desai

faqs.q: The Janata Government sought to undo many changes introduced by the 42nd Amendment Act (1976) through which two subsequent Amendment Acts?
The Verma Committee on Fundamental Duties of the Citizens, which identified existing legal provisions for the implementation of some Fundamental Duties, was set up in which year?

rows: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
Prevents disrespect to the Constitution, National Flag and National Anthem
Various criminal laws
Punish encouraging enmity between sections of people on grounds of language, race, place of birth, religion, etc.
Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
Punishes offences related to caste and religion (known as the Untouchability (Offences) Act till 1976)
Indian Penal Code (IPC)
Declares imputations/assertions prejudicial to national integration as punishable offences
Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967
Provides for declaring a communal organisation an unlawful association
Representation of the People Act, 1951
Disqualifies MPs/MLAs for corrupt practices such as soliciting votes on religious/caste/communal grounds
Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972
Prohibits trade in rare and endangered species
Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980
Checks indiscriminate deforestation and diversion of forest land
